sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Create an animated, non-interactive surfing pelican using html/3js

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

```js
export function taperedTube(curve, segments, radiusFn, radialSegments=12, closed=false){
  const frames = curve.computeFrenetFrames(segments, closed);
  const positions=[], normals=[], uvs=[], indices=[];
  for(let i=0;i<=segments;i++){
    const u=i/segments, r=radiusFn(u);
    const P=curve.getPointAt(u); // or getPoint
    const N=frames.normals[i], B=frames.binormals[i];
    for(let j=0;j<=radialSegments;j++){
      const v=j/radialSegments*Math.PI*2;
      const sin=Math.sin(v), cos=-Math.cos(v);
      const nx=cos*N.x+sin*B.x, ny=..., nz=...;
      normal.push(nx,ny,nz);
      position.push(P.x+r*nx, ...);
      uv.push(i/segments, j/radialSegments);
    }
  }
  indices...
}
```

Oh! The `skyRadiance` for reflection: R = reflect(-V, N). For a grazing view on flat water, R points up at a grazing angle → skyRadiance(R) with R.y small → mix(horizon, zenith, pow(y,0.5)) → horizon ✓ bright. So it should be bright...

# Dawn Patrol — a surfing pelican

An animated, non-interactive WebGL short film: a brown pelican trim-surfs a
longboard across a slow-motion dawn swell while a virtual camera flies a
never-repeating orbit around it. There are no controls — the page is a film.

## Run

```sh
npm install          # three.js
# dev: serve the folder and open index.html, or bundle once:
npx esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=bundle.js
```

`index.html` loads `main.js` as an ES module; everything (geometry, textures,
foam, sky) is generated in code — no external assets, no network, no storage.

## What's in the frame

- **The sea** is one analytic height field (six directional gravity-wave
  components in slow motion). The *same* parameter list is evaluated on the CPU
  — so the board, wake and camera sit exactly on the rendered surface — and
  code-generated into GLSL for displacement, analytic normals, capillary chop,
  fresnel sky reflection, backlit translucency, sun glitter and gated
  whitecaps. The mesh is a polar disc: 0.4-unit rings under the surfer widening
  to 50-unit rings at a 1.4 km horizon, so one seamless mesh covers everything.
- **The pelican** is built from lathes, tapered tubes and vertex-coloured wing
  grids (white coverts → grey → black primaries), with a gular pouch that gapes
  and jiggles, stabilised head gaze, balance-correcting wings with flap bursts,
  webbed feet planted in a surf stance, and a generated feather bump map.
- **The board** is an extruded outline with rocker, foil taper, vertex-painted
  livery, three fins, a traction pad and a leash cuffed to the back ankle. It
  rides a plane fitted to four wave probes, banks into carves and pumps with
  the swell.
- **Foam**: a GPU point-spray system (tail wash, rail fans through carves,
  nose-slam bursts), a trail ribbon that re-lies on the moving surface each
  frame, and a contact shadow that conforms to the local wave normal.
- **Sky & light**: procedural gradient dome with two masked cloud decks and a
  low sun; ACES tone mapping; gulls wheeling in the distance; a cinematic
  camera driven by layered incommensurate sines plus handheld drift.

## Files

| file | role |
| --- | --- |
| `main.js` | bootstrap: renderer, lights, world assembly, frame loop |
| `src/waves.js` | the shared wave field (CPU + generated GLSL) |
| `src/ocean.js` | polar sea mesh + water shader |
| `src/sky.js` | sky dome, sun, clouds |
| `src/pelican.js` | bird rig, plumage, animation |
| `src/board.js` | surfboard, fins, pad, leash |
| `src/surfer.js` | ride physics: path, wave-plane fit, carve bank, foam cues |
| `src/foam.js` | spray particles, wake ribbon, contact shadow, mist |
| `src/camera.js` | cinematic orbit rig |
| `src/gulls.js` | background flock |
| `src/textures.js` | canvas-generated bump/dot/shadow/speckle textures |
| `src/util.js`, `src/glsl-common.js` | math + shared GLSL noise |

Done. **Dawn Patrol** — an animated, non-interactive WebGL surf film starring a pelican on a longboard.

**What was built**

- `index.html` + `main.js` (ES module) + 12 modules in `src/`, `three` via npm, all textures/geometry generated in code (no assets, no network, no storage).
- **Sea**: one analytic swell field (6 directional gravity waves in slow-mo) evaluated identically on the CPU (board/wake/camera sit exactly on the surface) and code-generated into GLSL; polar-disc mesh (0.4-unit rings at the surfer → 50-unit rings at a 1.4 km horizon) with analytic normals, capillary chop, Schlick fresnel sky reflection (below-horizon rays sample dark sea, not bright sky), backlit translucency, sun glitter and noise-gated whitecaps.
- **Pelican**: lathe torso, S-curved tapered neck, gaping/jiggling gular pouch, hooked bill, stabilised head gaze, vertex-coloured wing grids (white coverts → black primaries) with wrist fold + fluttering primaries + flap bursts, balance-correcting dihedral, webbed feet in a surf stance, generated feather bump map.
- **Board**: extruded outline with rocker/foil, vertex-painted livery, fins, traction pad, leash to the back ankle; rides a wave-plane fitted from four probes, banks into carves, pumps with the swell.
- **Foam**: GPU point spray (tail wash, carve rail fans, nose-slam bursts), a wake ribbon re-projected onto the moving surface each frame, wave-conforming contact shadow.
- **Film**: procedural sky dome with masked cloud decks and low sun, ACES grade, CSS vignette/title card, distant gulls, and a never-repeating cinematic orbit with handheld drift — no user controls anywhere.

**Verification**: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm` passes; a node smoke test stepped 3600 sim frames with no NaNs; headless-Chrome renders (SwiftShader) confirmed shaders compile and the composition reads, and drove several art-direction fixes (water plaid, horizon aliasing, pelican proportions, camera occlusion). Dev-only harness files were removed afterwards.
